ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic благъ (blagŭ). Displaced the inherited East Slavic form, from Proto-Slavic *bolgъ (“good”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bordačь (“bearded man”). By surface analysis, борода́ (borodá, “beard”) + -ач (-ač).

s.g: leap year (366-day year in the Gregorian calendar)

s.g: Liberia (a country in West Africa, on the Atlantic Ocean, with Monrovia as its capital)

NKVD, the People’s Commissariat for Interior Affairs (a forerunner of the KGB).
to concern, to relate, to apply (to be relevant)
to wear out (of clothing, shoes, etc.)

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *služьba. By surface analysis, служи́ть (služítʹ) + -ба (-ba).

ety.text: Compounded from так (tak) + -с (-s), which is an abbreviated form of су́дарь (súdarʹ)/суда́рыня (sudárynja).

s.g: Any fish of the genus Gymnocorymbus.

ety.text: Borrowed from translingual ternetzi (as the specific epithet of Gymnocorymbus ternetzi). The species was named after ichthyologist Carl Ternetz (whence also Anostomus ternetzi and Liotyphlops ternetzii). The surname originates from the Slavic languages. Compare Терниц (Ternic), likely related to Russian те́рница (térnica), Ukrainian те́рниця (térnycja), possibly derived from an agricultural occupational surname.

s.g: Ukraine (a country in Eastern Europe, bordering on the north shore of the Black Sea)

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic оукра́ина (ukráina, “borderland”), from Proto-Slavic *ukrajina. By surface analysis, у- (u-) + край (kraj) + -ина (-ina).

s.g: check (on someone), control, justice (a way to control someone's wilful or lawless acts)
restitution, satisfaction (for an injury or loss)

x: За обе́дом запива́ли мы азиа́тский шашлы́к англи́йским пи́вом и шампа́нским, засты́вшим в снега́х таври́йских.

ety.text: Borrowed from Crimean Tatar şışlıq / шишлик (şişlik, “something to be cooked on a skewer”), from şiş (“spit, skewer”) + -lik (“-ness, -hood, -ity”; also “for”).

s.g: a female surname, Shulgina, masculine equivalent Шульги́н (Šulʹgín)

ety.text: From a finnic language, ultimately from Proto-Finnic *huudëh. Compare Finnish huude, Veps hudeg, Ludian huudeh
